---
title: "Nonlinear models with several variables"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, chapter 8, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

For a nonlinear model the recipe is to find the equilibria, compute the
Jacobian at each one, and apply the linear stability conditions from
chapter 7. `stability` does all three steps.

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
```

## Competition

In Lotka–Volterra competition, species 1 and 2 have carrying capacities
`K₁`, `K₂`. A competitor counts `α` (or `β`) times as much as a member of
one's own species.

```{julia}
@syms n₁::nonneg n₂::nonneg r₁::positive r₂::positive K₁::positive K₂::positive α::positive β::positive
comp = ode(n₁ => r₁ * n₁ * (1 - (n₁ + α * n₂) / K₁),
           n₂ => r₂ * n₂ * (1 - (n₂ + β * n₁) / K₂))
eqs = equilibria(comp)
```

Species 2 alone resists invasion by species 1 when `K₁ < α K₂`:

```{julia}
only2 = only(e for e in eqs if iszero(e[n₁]) && !iszero(e[n₂]))
stability(comp, only2)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert length(eqs) == 4
@assert isequiv(stability(comp, only2).condition, K₁ < α * K₂)
```

The coexistence equilibrium is stable when each species limits itself more
than it limits the other (here with numbers, `α = β = 1/2`):

```{julia}
co = only(e for e in eqs if !iszero(e[n₁]) && !iszero(e[n₂]))
sc = stability(comp, co)
decide(subs(sc.condition, α => 1 // 2, β => 1 // 2, K₁ => 1, K₂ => 1))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(co[n₁], (K₁ - α * K₂) / (1 - α * β))
@assert decide(subs(sc.condition, α => 1 // 2, β => 1 // 2, K₁ => 1, K₂ => 1)) === true
@assert decide(subs(sc.condition, α => 2, β => 2, K₁ => 1, K₂ => 1)) === false
```

## Predators and prey

In the Lotka–Volterra predator–prey model the interior equilibrium has purely
imaginary eigenvalues: a centre, which linear analysis cannot classify (the
verdict is `neutral`).

```{julia}
@syms N::nonneg P::nonneg r::positive b::positive c::positive d::positive K::positive
lv = ode(N => r * N - b * N * P, P => c * b * N * P - d * P)
inner = only(e for e in equilibria(lv) if !iszero(e[N]))
stability(lv, inner)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
sl = stability(lv, inner)
@assert sl.verdict === :neutral
@assert isequiv(inner[N], d / (c * b)) && isequiv(inner[P], r / b)
```

Logistic growth of the prey turns the centre into a stable equilibrium
whenever the equilibrium is feasible (positive):

```{julia}
rm = ode(N => r * N * (1 - N / K) - b * N * P, P => c * b * N * P - d * P)
inner2 = only(e for e in equilibria(rm) if !iszero(e[N]) && !iszero(e[P]))
```

```{julia}
s2 = stability(rm, inner2)
s2.condition
```

```{julia}
assuming(c * b * K > d) do        # the predator can persist
    decide(s2.condition)
end
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert assuming(() -> decide(s2.condition), c * b * K > d) === true
```

## An epidemic with births and deaths

In an SIR model with recruitment `Λ`, transmission `β`, recovery `γ` and death
rate `μ`, the disease-free equilibrium is stable when `R₀ < 1`, and the
endemic one exists and is stable when `R₀ > 1`.

```{julia}
@syms S::nonneg I::nonneg Λ::positive β::positive γ::positive μ::positive
sir = ode(S => Λ - β * S * I - μ * S, I => β * S * I - (γ + μ) * I)
equilibria(sir)
```

```{julia}
dfe = Dict(S => Λ / μ, I => 0)
R₀ = reproduction_number([β * S * I], [(γ + μ) * I], [I], dfe)
```

```{julia}
stability(sir, dfe).condition
```

```{julia}
endemic = only(e for e in equilibria(sir) if !iszero(e[I]))
se = stability(sir, endemic)
assuming(β * Λ > μ * (γ + μ)) do   # R₀ > 1
    decide(se.condition)
end
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(R₀, β * Λ / (μ * (γ + μ)))
@assert isequiv(stability(sir, dfe).condition, β * Λ < μ * (γ + μ))
@assert isequiv(endemic[S], (γ + μ) / β)
@assert assuming(() -> decide(se.condition), β * Λ > μ * (γ + μ)) === true
```
